text:
[LGRA.10.1.4] **A `withdraw` in a nested body removes the fact the outer rule
matched, and only that fact.** `withdraw b` may stand in a body nested in an
action: a call continuation, an error or timeout body, or an `after` body.
It runs when that body runs, and it removes the fact the outer rule had bound
to `b` when it fired. If that fact is no longer in working memory when the
body runs — withdrawn, expired, or replaced by a meaningful change, which
makes the replacement a different fact ([LFAC.2.5.3]) — the action does
nothing. The engine **must not** withdraw a fact that has taken the matched
fact's place under the same identity key: the rule never saw it.

The removal is the author's own withdrawal, recorded as such ([RFCS.7a.2]).
Its sequencing within the body is [LGRA.10.1.3]'s.
